reasons: Debug mode and a development secret key are written into the generated settings file.
The command helper never reports failure because it does not raise errors when check is off, so the script always says success.
The frontend folder is created but not filled, so the UI step may do nothing.

terms.meaning: A database stored in a single file, needing no server.
A private folder of Python packages for this project.
A command started by the script from inside Python, such as a pip install.
A setting that shows extra detail and may expose internal errors. It should be off in real use.
The place where a program starts running when it is launched directly.

used_by: Run by the owner from the project folder.
start_app.sh or start_app.bat (created by this script).

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Script setup and Windows encoding fix
sections.what: Imports the standard tools the script needs and, on Windows only, makes the output able to print emoji and other symbols.
sections.why: Without this fix, the emoji messages can crash the script on some Windows consoles.
sections.watch_out: The fix replaces the output streams, so anything else that writes to the console in this script must use the same settings.

sections.name: print_header
sections.title: Header printer
sections.what: Prints a line of equal signs, the text, and another line, to separate sections of output.
sections.why: Makes the progress readable in the terminal.
sections.watch_out: Only affects display, so changing it does not change any setup behaviour.

sections.name: run_command
sections.title: Command runner
sections.what: Runs a shell command, prints its normal output, and prints its errors if it fails.
sections.why: Lets the setup run pip and other commands without writing each one out by hand.
sections.watch_out: Because the failure check is off in most calls, this helper returns success even when the command failed. Only real exceptions are caught, and those are not raised here.

sections.name: main (part 1)
sections.title: Start checks and virtual environment
sections.what: Checks the Python version is 3.11 or newer, creates the virtual environment if it is missing, and picks the correct activation and install commands for the operating system.
sections.why: The rest of the script needs the right Python and command paths for Windows or Mac and Linux.
sections.watch_out: Commands run from this script use the Python that started it, so running it with an old Python can cause a wrong install.

sections.name: main (part 2)
sections.title: Package list and settings file
sections.what: Writes a short package list, installs it, and then either checks an existing settings file or creates a new one. For a new file it asks for an OpenAI key and writes it, along with other default settings.
sections.why: The app needs its packages and an OpenAI key before it can run.
sections.watch_out: The generated settings file sets debug mode on and uses a weak development secret, which should be changed before any real use.

sections.name: main (part 3)
sections.title: Database table creation
sections.what: Writes a temporary script that creates all the database tables, runs it, and then deletes it.
sections.why: The app needs its tables before it can save anything.
sections.watch_out: The message on failure says it may be normal, so a real failure can be missed.

sections.name: main (part 4)
sections.title: Model list, frontend folder and start scripts
sections.what: Loads the model list through a temporary script, creates the frontend folder, and writes a start script for the operating system that launches the backend on port 8000 and a simple web server on port 3000.
sections.why: Gives the owner a single file to double-click or run to start everything.
sections.watch_out: The frontend folder is created empty, so the page on port 3000 may show nothing until real frontend files are added.

sections.name: main (part 5)
sections.title: Summary of created files
sections.what: Prints a list of the files and folders created, plus the start command for the operating system.
sections.why: Tells the owner what changed on their computer.
sections.watch_out: The list is printed whether or not each step truly worked.

sections.name: main (part 6)
sections.title: Usage and reminder messages
sections.what: Prints the start command, the web addresses for the UI and API docs, the documentation names, and reminders to back up the database file and keep the key secret.
sections.why: Gives the owner the next steps after setup.
sections.watch_out: The documentation file names listed here are not checked by the script and may not exist.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Program entry point and error handling
sections.what: Runs the main setup when the file is started directly, handles Ctrl+C by stopping cleanly, and prints the full error details for any other failure.
sections.why: Lets the owner see what went wrong instead of a silent crash.
sections.watch_out: Any error raised in the setup stops the whole run, so later steps are skipped.

summary: A cross-platform Python script that installs a simpler version of the platform using a single SQLite file, writes a settings file, and creates scripts to start the app.
purpose: Lets the owner run the platform on Windows, Mac or Linux with no database server to install.
why: Likely reason: PostgreSQL and Docker are hard to install on some computers, so a file-based database is an easier start.
how: The script checks Python is 3.11 or newer, creates a virtual environment, writes a small package list and installs it. It asks for an OpenAI key and writes the settings file. It then creates the database tables and the model list through short temporary scripts, creates a frontend folder, and writes a start script for the operating system.
inputs: An OpenAI API key typed at the prompt, and the current folder layout.
outputs: A virtual environment, a survey_data.db file, a settings file, a start script, and a frontend folder.
risks: The generated settings file turns on debug mode and uses a weak secret key. Install steps print an error but still report success. The frontend folder is created empty, so the UI may not appear.
debug: If the start script fails, run the backend command directly from the backend folder to see the error. If the database is empty, rerun the table step. If packages are missing, reinstall them from the package list. Look at survey_data.db to confirm the tables exist.
